_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4b, IC4-R1). `pairs` is the plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides. The confused pairings (Ney/Lannes, Massena/Davout) drawn twice each.

who.Ney: Ney — a bold marshal, famous for his courage and his impatience to fight.
who.Davout: Davout — a careful marshal, strict, exact, who counts every man and never wastes one.
who.Murat: Murat — a bold cavalry marshal who loves to ride and charge.
who.Lannes: Lannes — a bold marshal who marches to the sound of the guns and leads assaults himself.
who.Massena: Masséna — a stubborn marshal who never gives up ground he holds.
who.Bernadotte: Bernadotte — a slow, politic marshal who is never in a hurry and always has an excuse.

pairs.line1: No task, Sire? I'll find a fight myself now, before I go mad sitting here.
pairs.line2: As I see fit, Sire. Wherever the guns are loudest, that's where you'll find me.

pairs.line1: Boldly? At last, Sire — no more sitting still, I go now.
pairs.line2: Boldly, Sire? Straight at them with the columns.

pairs.line1: Give me a post, Sire, with the rolls and stores to match. I'll see every man fed.
pairs.line2: Leave me here, Sire. This is my ground, and they pay for every yard.

pairs.line1: A victory. I'll accept slightly worse odds now, once the rolls are counted.
pairs.line2: A victory, Sire. What we won stays mine, and I'll risk a little more.

pairs.line1: It went badly, Sire. Give me another go; I'd sooner be fighting than brooding.
pairs.line2: It did not succeed, Sire. Circumstances were against me.

pairs.line1: Nothing to trouble you with, Sire. I'm sure you have worries enough.
pairs.line2: No guns near me yet, Sire.

pairs.line1: Carefully, then. I'll sit on my ground and not give an inch.
pairs.line2: Carefully, Sire. But if I hear the guns, I go to them.

pairs.line1: Bolder, then. I'll still count every man I send.
pairs.line2: Boldly? If you insist, Sire, though I'm sure you'll want the risks weighed.

pairs.line1: You called me back last time, Sire. Let me see this one through.
pairs.line2: You gave another man the ground that was mine to take, Sire. I remember it.

pairs.line1: Bored of this, Sire. The horses and I have changed it.
pairs.line2: The same again, Sire? I've changed the routine and recounted every man.

pairs.line1: Nothing worth chasing yet, Sire. Let me hold here with the horses saddled.
pairs.line2: Nothing in reach to hit, Sire. I'm restless, but I'll hold here until something comes.

pairs.line1: Bolder still? Give me the squadrons and a loose rein.
pairs.line2: Bolder, Sire? I'll need a comfortable moment to think how that might be done safely.

rows.line: No excuses, Sire. Send me at the next one and I'll storm it.
It was not enough. I'll check the rolls, Sire, and do it right.
I failed you, Sire. Let me try again today; I can't sit and brood.
It went wrong, Sire. I held my ground as long as I could.
I regret it, Sire. The conditions were poor.
The ride did not go as I pictured it, Sire.
We won, Sire. The field is mine now, and I'll hold it.
A victory, Sire. A little more ambition seems affordable now.
We won, Sire. I've counted the losses, and I'll allow a little more risk.
We beat them, Sire. I'll go in sooner next time.
Another win, Sire. The horses and I will ride farther now.
We won, Sire. Next time I'll storm harder.
It changed, so I stayed on my ground. Nobody takes it from me.
No move today, Sire. Things changed, and my figures no longer held.
The chance closed before I could get a squadron across.
I thought it better not to move, Sire. Matters had changed.
The guns told me it had changed, so I held the columns.
Not this time, Sire. It galls me to sit still, but the chance was gone.
Moving forward, Sire. What I pass is mine, and I keep it.
On the road, Sire, with plenty of rests. We'll arrive when we arrive.
The columns marched today, Sire. I like to be near where it starts.
On his heels, Sire. He can hear us coming.
We marched in good order, Sire. Every man counted, no stragglers.
The men are moving, Sire. I'd have them run now if I could.
I'd keep this ground, Sire. It's mine now, and worth keeping.
No friend near the guns, Sire. Let me hold here and listen for them.
Let me stay in the rear, Sire, where the men are comfortable. Someone must.
Let me hold and watch the roads, Sire. The first dust I see, I'm after it.
Let me dig in here, Sire, and see every man fed and in his place.
I'll hold here if I must, Sire, but I'm restless. Let me loose the moment something shows.
